faq.a: Wahid is associated with the Arabic form وَاحِد, whose core sense is wahid; one, unique.

faq.q: What is the origin of Wahid?
faq.a: Wahid is associated with Arabic. Wahid is Arabic وَاحِد (Wāḥid), meaning 'one, unique'.
Yes — the underlying form وَاحِد is Arabic.
Wahid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Wahid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root و ح د is Quranic (oneness), but Wāḥid is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Wahid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Wahid is rendered واحد and carries the sense واحد، ایک.

faq.q: What does Wahid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Wahid is rendered واحد and carries the sense واحد، یکتا.
A romanized syllable approximation is wa-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Wahid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Wahid, wahid. Script forms are واحد, وَاحِد, वाहिद.

faq.q: Is Wahid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
